summary: The SEV-1 spike in HTTP 500s on POST /v1/orders was caused by dep-5101, the 12:10:00Z deployment of order-service v2.14.0, which introduced a new MarginCheckValidator into the order validation chain for F&O orders. For derivatives orders the new validator dereferences a null marginProfile and throws NullPointerException at MarginCheckValidator.java:88, failing the request with HTTP 500. Confidence is high (0.85 per reviewed ranking, critic-raised to 0.90): the untruncated error set partitions exhaustively into 103 MarginCheckValidator NPEs + 88 "marginProfile is null" rejections, all 100% orderType=FNO with zero CASH/EQUITY signatures, and onset (12:10-12:11Z bucket, first ERROR 12:12:31Z) falls 1-2 minutes after the deploy with no other change in the window. Alternative dependency, saturation and config causes are each contradicted by direct evidence (flat latency and resources, zero downstream WARN+, off-path config change). The deploy was atomic with no canary stages, no feature flag, and has not been rolled back as of 13:59Z.

ranked_hypotheses.title: dep-5101 introduced a broken F&O margin validation path yielding NPE on FNO orders
ranked_hypotheses.statement: order-service v2.14.0 (dep-5101, deployed 12:10:00Z) replaced legacy OrderRules.validateMargin() with a new MarginCheckValidator in the validation chain. For derivatives (FNO) orders the new validator dereferences a null marginProfile and throws NullPointerException at MarginCheckValidator.java:88, so the request fails with HTTP 500. Cash/equity orders never traverse this FNO branch, so the blast radius is derivatives-only. The fault originates in the deployed order-service release, not in any dependency. Residual uncertainty is confined to the exact origin of the null marginProfile (own code vs. an uninspected upstream supplier) and to rollout-completion timing; neither changes the top ranking.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5101 deploys order-service v2.14.0 at 12:10:00Z, adding MarginCheckValidator to the validation chain and removing legacy OrderRules.validateMargin(); it is the only deployment across all services in the window, with no rollout/canary stages.
The new validator is on the order-placement path and is reached only for F&O (derivatives) order types; it is not feature-flag-gated and no flag service exists in the topology.
marginProfile is null for the offending accounts, so MarginCheckValidator.validate dereferences null at line 88 and raises NullPointerException (the data supplier of marginProfile was not inspected).

The NPE surfaces as an order rejection / HTTP 500: the untruncated 191-entry ERROR set partitions exhaustively into 103 FNO MarginCheckValidator NPEs + 88 'order rejected with 500: marginProfile is null'.

order-service 5xx error rate steps from ~0.2% to ~18% at the 12:10-12:11Z buckets, 1-2 minutes after the deploy, matching the first ERROR log at 12:12:31Z; onset is pinned to 12:10-12:11Z, not the earlier cfg-2101 minute.
Failures are 100% FNO: filtering ERROR entries by orderType=CASH and orderType=EQUITY both return 0, so cash/equity orders are genuinely unaffected, matching the deploy's stated F&O scope.
api-gateway error rate rises in the same window by roughly an order of magnitude less, consistent with it merely relaying failing order traffic.

No dependency-side fault is present: exchange-gateway and pricing-engine show zero WARN+ logs in 11:55-12:25Z over complete ranges, and pricing-engine/payment-service/settlement-service/user-db error rates and latency are flat through onset.

assumptions: That the null marginProfile arises from within order-service's own new code path (unpopulated field, changed mapping, or removal of a legacy fallback in validateMargin) rather than from an uninspected upstream supplier returning nothing. The NPE's location inside MarginCheckValidator makes the former overwhelmingly more likely, but no margin-service exists in the catalog and ledger-db/redis were not queried, so the supplier of margin profiles was never directly inspected.

That order-service v2.14.0 had finished rolling out and was receiving FNO traffic by 12:10-12:12Z. Deploy completion logs were not retrievable; the error onset 1-2 minutes after the deploy timestamp is consistent with, but not direct proof of, rollout completion.

That the removed OrderRules.validateMargin() did contain an F&O fallback the new path dropped - the changelog exposes only two summary lines with no line-level diff (F22); the only evidence is the runtime NPE itself.
That the FNO share of traffic is at least ~18%, sufficient to produce the observed sustained error rate from an FNO-only failure (no product-type mix metric exists).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Downstream dependency (exchange-gateway / pricing-engine / shared DB-queue) degradation surfaces as 500s on derivatives orders
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A dependency on the order-placement path - exchange-gateway, pricing-engine, or a shared component (ledger-db, kafka, redis-cache) behind them - degraded around 12:10Z, and order-service therefore returned 500s. Because derivatives orders touch deeper/margin-related downstream calls, the failures present as FNO-specific.

causal_chain.claim: order-service outbound dependencies are ledger-db, pricing-engine, exchange-gateway and kafka; several are shared, so a neighbour's fault can reach order-service.
One of these dependencies degrades around onset, causing order calls to fail.
Failures concentrate on derivatives orders because those calls are deeper/slower on the dependency path.
order-service surfaces the dependency failure as HTTP 500 on POST /v1/orders.

assumptions: That a dependency could degrade without emitting any WARN+ log, without leaving a change trace in an otherwise complete global change window, and while producing a NullPointerException inside caller-side validation code.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Contradicted by direct evidence. The observed error is a hard NullPointerException raised inside order-service's own newly deployed MarginCheckValidator (F9, F14, F24), not a timeout, connection-refused or upstream-error propagation that a dependency fault produces. latency_p99 is flat at ~148-153ms including onset (F10) with no resource/pool saturation (F13), ruling out dependency-induced blocking. exchange-gateway and pricing-engine logs contain zero WARN+ entries in 11:55-12:25Z over a complete data range (F15), and pricing-engine error_rate is flat with no onset (F30). payment-service, settlement-service and user-db are also flat across onset (F28, F29, F31, F32). Failures are 100% orderType=FNO with 0 cash/equity signatures (F25), matching the deploy's stated F&O scope rather than a dependency call pattern. No corresponding change exists in the window (F1, F3).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Local resource exhaustion / saturation in order-service or a shared datastore
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Connection pool, thread pool, memory or DB-connection exhaustion - possibly triggered by the heavier derivatives order flow - produced intermittent 500s that disproportionately hit F&O orders.

causal_chain.claim: Heavier derivatives order flow consumes pool/thread/memory resources.
Resources exhaust, so order requests fail intermittently, concentrated on the heavier FNO path.
Failures surface as HTTP 500 on POST /v1/orders.

assumptions: That an unmeasured resource (e.g. thread pool, GC pauses) could exhaust while CPU, memory, db pool and restarts all stay flat.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Directly contradicted: cpu_pct flat ~40%, memory_pct flat ~60%, db_pool_in_use flat (max 15.17, no climb), restarts identically 0 across all buckets, and latency_p99 flat ~148-153ms through onset (F13, F10). request_rate is flat and normal (~233 req/s, no step at onset), so there is no traffic surge (F26). Saturation would show climbing pool/latency; neither exists. The error is a deterministic NPE on a specific new code path and 100% FNO (F9, F14, F25), not an intermittent allocation/timeout failure.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Non-deploy cause: config change, credential expiry, or shared-platform/infra change
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A configuration change, expired credential/secret, or shared platform component (mesh/gateway/auth/config service) changed around onset and broke order placement across services, with order-service merely the first alerting and derivatives tickets being a reporting artifact.

causal_chain.claim: A shared platform or off-path config change affects order placement at 12:10Z.
order-service 500s and api-gateway errors follow, with derivatives tickets merely over-reported by traders.

assumptions: That a config change off the order path or an unobserved credential/platform change could produce an NPE inside a newly deployed class at exactly the deploy's minute.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: cfg-2101 is notification-service email.batch_size, not on the order path, and occurred 49 minutes before onset with no order-path linkage (F3, F16). Onset is pinned to 12:10-12:11Z, exactly the dep-5101 minute, not 11:21Z (F8, F16). Error logs are 100% orderType=FNO and point at MarginCheckValidator.java:88 - a code-level signature, not a config/credential failure mode (F9, F14, F24). A shared-platform fault would be expected to degrade neighbours too, but portfolio-service is flat at ~0.2% throughout (F12), pricing-engine/payment-service/settlement-service/user-db are flat (F28-F32), and api-gateway's rise is an order-of-magnitude-smaller propagation artifact (F11). No past incident matches a margin/validation change or F&O rejection signature (F6).

Downstream dependencies on the order path show no independent fault at onset: exchange-gateway and pricing-engine logs contain zero WARN+ entries in 11:55-12:25Z over complete data ranges, and pricing-engine error_rate is flat with no onset.

Neighbouring services are flat across the onset window: payment-service error_rate and latency flat (0.16-0.29%, ~304-333ms), settlement-service flat (0.16-0.25%), user-db health flat (slow queries ~0.2-0.38/min, connections ~25, replication lag ~30ms), and portfolio-service flat ~0.2% throughout.

recommended_actions.action: Immediately roll back dep-5101 (order-service v2.14.0) to the prior release; the record is still status 'live' with rolled_back_at null, so rollback has not yet been performed.
recommended_actions.rationale: The failing code path (MarginCheckValidator at MarginCheckValidator.java:88) exists only in v2.14.0, deployed 12:10:00Z. Removing the deployment removes the fault. Precedent HIST-109 resolved a validation-code regression the same way. The deploy is atomic with no flag gate, so rollback is the only available kill switch.

recommended_actions.action: While the rollback propagates, consider pausing or rejecting FNO order placements at the api-gateway/order-service boundary (or draining FNO traffic) to stop customer-visible 500s.
recommended_actions.rationale: Blast radius is measured to be exactly 100% orderType=FNO with 0 CASH/EQUITY errors, so isolating derivatives traffic protects customers without affecting unaffected product lines.

recommended_actions.action: Verify recovery after rollback: confirm order-service error_rate returns to ~0.2% baseline and that MarginCheckValidator NPE entries cease in the 12:12:31Z signature.
recommended_actions.rationale: Error rate was flat ~0.2% pre-deploy and ~18% post-deploy with a code-level NPE signature; recovery should restore both signals, providing a clean before/after confirmation.

recommended_actions.action: Fix MarginCheckValidator.validate to null-guard the marginProfile and restore the legacy OrderRules.validateMargin() F&O fallback semantics before re-releasing v2.14.0.
recommended_actions.rationale: The NPE at line 88 dereferences a null marginProfile for FNO orders; the removed validateMargin() path is the legacy behavior that the new path must not have dropped. No line-level diff was available, so the fallback behavior must be confirmed in source rather than from the changelog.

recommended_actions.action: Add automated F&O-path integration/contract tests (derivatives order placement with a null/absent marginProfile) and require them in CI before order-validation changes ship.
recommended_actions.rationale: The regression is a deterministic NPE on the FNO branch that cash/equity tests would never exercise, and it reached production undetected.

recommended_actions.action: Introduce a feature flag or canary/staged rollout for order-validation changes so a bad path can be disabled without a full deploy.
recommended_actions.rationale: dep-5101 was an atomic live deploy with no canary stages and no flag record, so there was no isolation mechanism short of rollback for a validated NPE regression.

recommended_actions.action: Add a product-type (FNO vs cash) request/error breakdown metric to order-service dashboards, and alert on per-product-type error rate.
recommended_actions.rationale: The observed ~11-18% error rate could only be indirectly attributed to the FNO traffic share because no product-type mix metric exists, delaying precise blast-radius confirmation.

This limits certainty on whether the null marginProfile originates in order-service's own code versus an uninspected supplier -- though the NPE location inside MarginCheckValidator makes the former far more likely.

what_would_change_the_conclusion: Evidence that the null marginProfile is supplied by an uninspected upstream dependency (e.g. ledger-db, redis-cache or a margin-profile data source returning null) degrading at 12:10Z with its own WARN+/latency/error signature, which would shift causality off dep-5101's own code.

Observation that the same MarginCheckValidator NPE signature occurs in a deployment other than dep-5101, or that FNO NPEs predate the 12:10:00Z deploy, which would break the cause-precedes-effect chain.

A line-level diff showing the removed OrderRules.validateMargin() had no F&O fallback and that MarginCheckValidator is unchanged from a previously healthy release, which would undermine the 'new code path introduced the fault' claim.
Discovery that order-service v2.14.0 was not actually serving FNO traffic until well after 12:12Z (e.g. a staged rollout), which would weaken the tight temporal coupling between deploy and onset.

Evidence of an independent fault at a shared dependency (ledger-db, redis-cache, kafka) at 12:10Z with a matching error/latency step, which could indicate a contributing shared-infra cause alongside or instead of the code regression.

Proof that MarginCheckValidator is in fact gated behind an undocumented/in-code switch that was flipped at 12:10Z, which would reframe the trigger as a configuration action rather than the deployed code.

The order-service error signature at onset is precisely the new code path introduced by dep-5101: 16 ERROR entries in 12:05-12:20Z all read 'NullPointerException at MarginCheckValidator.validate(MarginCheckValidator.java:88) orderType=FNO', first at 2026-03-03T12:12:31Z, 100% FNO (derivatives). Reverting/isolating the validator would explain the derivatives-only failures: every observed failure enters through MarginCheckValidator.validate on orderType=FNO, the same call removed OrderRules.validateMargin(), and no cash/equity signature appears. Since no other service (api-gateway aside, as a propagation artifact) degrades and the failure is a hard NPE raised inside the new validation code path (not a timeout/connection error), the failures are localized to the deployed component rather than a shared dependency.
